    name: Quality gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes, static, flutter-analyze, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, model-switch-reg, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, perf-gate, usage-fold, cli-visual-settings, cube-kernel-live, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos, integration-mock, hostile-env, fa-aot-build, pty-integration-linux, pty-coverage-gate, pty-visual, supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-portability, installer-verify, install-pin-gate, flutter-app-exzone, flutter-app-goldens, flutter-app-lock-smoke, office-addin-suite, extension-size-gate]
    if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    # #1368: the publish job consumes dart_ok — the pure-Dart package verdict
    # — instead of this aggregate's result. The aggregate itself stays the
    # single required check: any red leg (platform included) still fails it.
    outputs:
      dart_ok: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.dart_ok }}
    steps:
      - name: Report leg results
        run: |
          echo "static        = ${{ needs.static.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "test-core     = ${{ needs.test-core.result }}"
          echo "coverage-gate = ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "guards        = ${{ needs.guards.result }}"
          echo "flutter-analyze = ${{ needs.flutter-analyze.result }}"
          echo "flutter-tests = ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}"
          echo "test-faui     = ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}"
          echo "app-crap-gate = ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}"
          echo "perf-gate     = ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}"
          echo "usage-fold    = ${{ needs.usage-fold.result }}"
          echo "cube-live     = ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}"
          echo "cli-visual    = ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}"
          echo "build-web     = ${{ needs.build-web.result }}"
          echo "build-android = ${{ needs.build-android.result }}"
          echo "build-ios     = ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}"
          echo "build-macos   = ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}"
          echo "integ-mock    = ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "pty-integ-linux = ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}"
          echo "fa-aot-build  = ${{ needs.fa-aot-build.result }}"
          echo "pty-gates     = ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "pty-visual    = ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}"
          echo "supply-chain  = ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}"
          echo "dep-audit     = ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}"
          echo "installer-it = ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}"
          echo "installer-reg  = ${{ needs.installer-portability.result }}"
          echo "pin-gate    = ${{ needs.install-pin-gate.result }}"
          echo "exzone      = ${{ needs.flutter-app-exzone.result }}"
          echo "goldens     = ${{ needs.flutter-app-goldens.result }}"
          echo "lock-smoke  = ${{ needs.flutter-app-lock-smoke.result }}"
          echo "office-addin  = ${{ needs.office-addin-suite.result }}"
          echo "ext-size-gate = ${{ needs.extension-size-gate.result }}"
          echo "model-switch-reg = ${{ needs.model-switch-reg.result }}"
      - name: Fail on any real failure (skipped security = dodge = FAIL)
        id: gate
        env:
          R_CHANGES: ${{ needs.changes.result }}
          R_SUPPLY_CHAIN: ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}
          R_DEP_AUDIT: ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}
          R_STATIC: ${{ needs.static.result }}
          R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE: ${{ needs.flutter-analyze.result }}
          R_TEST_CORE: ${{ needs.test-core.result }}
          R_COVERAGE: ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}
          R_GUARDS: ${{ needs.guards.result }}
          R_FLUTTER: ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}
          R_CRAP: ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}
          R_FAUI: ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}
          R_PERF: ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}
          R_USAGE_FOLD: ${{ needs.usage-fold.result }}
          R_CUBE: ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}
          R_CLI_VISUAL: ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}
          R_BUILD_WEB: ${{ needs.build-web.result }}
          R_BUILD_ANDROID: ${{ needs.build-android.result }}
          R_BUILD_IOS: ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}
          R_BUILD_MACOS: ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}
          R_INTEG: ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}
          R_HOSTILE: ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}
          R_PTY_LINUX: ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}
          R_FA_AOT: ${{ needs.fa-aot-build.result }}
          R_PTY_GATES: ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}
          R_PTY_VISUAL: ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}
          R_INSTALLER_VERIFY: ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}
          R_INSTALLER_REG: ${{ needs.installer-portability.result }}
          R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE: ${{ needs.install-pin-gate.result }}
          R_EXZONE: ${{ needs.flutter-app-exzone.result }}
          R_GOLDENS: ${{ needs.flutter-app-goldens.result }}
          R_LOCK_SMOKE: ${{ needs.flutter-app-lock-smoke.result }}
          R_OFFICE_ADDIN: ${{ needs.office-addin-suite.result }}
          R_EXT_SIZE: ${{ needs.extension-size-gate.result }}
          R_MODEL_SWITCH_REG: ${{ needs.model-switch-reg.result }}
        run: |
          fail() { echo "Quality gate FAILED: $1"; exit 1; }
          # Verdict pass collects blockers WITHOUT exiting, so dart_ok is
          # always exported explicitly ('true' or 'false', never '') —
          # publish and the Provider smoke read this output and an empty
          # value must never read as either (review thread on #1370).
          dart_blocker=""
          # The classifier itself must have run: a failed or skipped
          # classifier skips EVERY downstream leg and would wave a PR
          # through with zero gates executed.
          [ "$R_CHANGES" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="changes classifier = $R_CHANGES"
          # Security legs must EXECUTE and pass. For these, skipped is a
          # dodge (e.g. a cunning diff that makes the classifier misfire),
          # not a pass — review follow-up, #796/#801.
          if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
            [ "$R_SUPPLY_CHAIN" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="supply-chain = $R_SUPPLY_CHAIN (skipped security is a dodge)"
          fi
          if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
            [ "$R_DEP_AUDIT" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="dep-audit = $R_DEP_AUDIT (skipped security is a dodge)"
          fi
          # #1368 — two independent verdicts over the needs legs:
          #   PACKAGE legs (everything NOT platform) → dart_blocker: they
          #     gate dart_ok AND the aggregate — analyze/test/coverage must
          #     gate the publish (review thread: the case bodies were
          #     swapped in the first cut, re-enshrining the starvation);
          #   PLATFORM/NATIVE/PTY legs (build-web/android/ios/macos,
          #     fa-aot-build, installer-verify, install-pin-gate,
          #     cube-kernel-live, cli-visual-settings, pty-*) → platform_red
          #     only: they redden the required aggregate but NEVER dart_ok —
          #     a red Windows build must not hold the pure-Dart publish
          #     hostage (the v1.0.519-521 starvation).
          platform_red=false
          for kv in "static:$R_STATIC" "flutter-analyze:$R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE" "test-core:$R_TEST_CORE" "coverage-gate:$R_COVERAGE" \
                    "guards:$R_GUARDS" "flutter-tests:$R_FLUTTER" "app-crap-gate:$R_CRAP" \
                    "test-faui:$R_FAUI" "perf-gate:$R_PERF" "usage-fold:$R_USAGE_FOLD" "cube-kernel-live:$R_CUBE" \
                    "cli-visual-settings:$R_CLI_VISUAL" "build-web:$R_BUILD_WEB" \
                    "build-android:$R_BUILD_ANDROID" "build-ios:$R_BUILD_IOS" "build-macos:$R_BUILD_MACOS" \
                    "integration-mock:$R_INTEG" "hostile-env:$R_HOSTILE" \
                    "fa-aot-build:$R_FA_AOT" \
                    "pty-integration-linux:$R_PTY_LINUX" "pty-coverage-gate:$R_PTY_GATES" "pty-visual:$R_PTY_VISUAL" \
                    "installer-portability:$R_INSTALLER_REG" \
                    "installer-verify:$R_INSTALLER_VERIFY" "install-pin-gate:$R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE" \
                    "model-switch-reg:$R_MODEL_SWITCH_REG" \
                    "flutter-app-exzone:$R_EXZONE" "flutter-app-goldens:$R_GOLDENS" "flutter-app-lock-smoke:$R_LOCK_SMOKE" "office-addin-suite:$R_OFFICE_ADDIN" "extension-size-gate:$R_EXT_SIZE"; do
            name="${kv%%:*}"; r="${kv#*:}"
            case "$name" in
              build-web|build-android|build-ios|build-macos|fa-aot-build|installer-verify|install-pin-gate|cube-kernel-live|cli-visual-settings|pty-integration-linux|pty-coverage-gate|pty-visual|flutter-app-lock-smoke|flutter-app-goldens|installer-portability|office-addin-suite|extension-size-gate)
                if [ "$r" != "success" ] && [ "$r" != "skipped" ]; then
                  platform_red=true
                fi
                ;;
              *)
                if [ "$r" != "success" ] && [ "$r" != "skipped" ] && [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
                  dart_blocker="a leg is $r ($name)"
                fi
                ;;
            esac
          done
          if [ -n "$dart_blocker" ]; then dart_ok=false; else dart_ok=true; fi
          echo "dart_ok=$dart_ok" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # Aggregate verdicts AFTER the export — branch protection is
          # unchanged: ANY red leg (package or platform) still fails this
          # required check; only the PUBLISH gate ignores platform reds.
          [ -z "$dart_blocker" ] || fail "$dart_blocker"
          [ "$platform_red" = "false" ] || fail "a platform/native leg is red — the aggregate is red; dart_ok stays true (publish is not gated on platform legs, #1368), see the leg results above"
          echo "Quality gate OK"

  # Issue #303 (the #262 DoD): the perf-tagged e2e gate must red-block the
  # MERGE, not only the release — before #551 the only integration leg
  # outside PRs was tag-time, and perf stays excluded from integration-mock.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  SHARED FAST GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL   ║
# ║  loc ≤ 2800 lines (crap4dart) · analyze · tests · coverage ≥ 80% ·        ║
# ║  duplication < 1% (flutter_app < 3.7%) · cross-module < 0.31%             ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# THE shared fast gate used by BOTH the pre-commit hook and CI (issue #177,
# AC7). Both callers run this exact script and diff the one-line markers
#   GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>
# for hook/CI parity. Every known stage ALWAYS prints exactly one marker:
# OK when it ran and passed, SKIP <reason> when it was not selected or a
# required tool is missing. A failing stage aborts the script with exit 1
# BEFORE its OK marker is printed (marker absent = failed).
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh [--scope auto|all|core|app|docs] [--stages list] [--hook]
#
#   --scope auto  Derive the scope from changed paths (default):
#                 - in a git hook (--hook flag or GIT_INDEX_FILE set):
#                   staged files via `git diff --cached --name-only`;
#                 - in CI (BASE_REF + HEAD_REF env vars set):
#                   `git diff --name-only $BASE_REF...$HEAD_REF`;
#                 - otherwise: "all" (safe default).
#   --scope all   Run every stage.
#   --scope core  analyze + test-core + coverage + crap + dup + dupx.
#   --scope app   analyze + dup + dupx + flutter.
#   --scope docs  analyze only.
#   --stages l    Comma-separated stage list; overrides the scope-derived set.
#                 Known stages: analyze,test-core,coverage,crap,dup,dupx,flutter,integration-mock
#
#
# Path rules (union logic, E1; test/** counts as core, E6):
#   docs/ | *.md | prompts/ .................. analyze
#   lib/ | bin/ | test/ | pubspec.* .......... + test-core, coverage, crap, dup, dupx
#   test/integration/** ...................... + integration-mock (no-key legs,
#                                              MockLlmServer; issue #551)
#   flutter_app/ | packages/ ................. + dup, dupx, flutter
#   scripts/ | .github/ | crap4dart.yaml ..... ALL stages (safe default, E2)
#   anything unknown ......................... ALL stages (safe default)
#
# Concurrency overrides: FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY / FA_FLUTTER_TEST_CONCURRENCY
# (auto-throttled via detect_test_concurrency, same as scripts/pre-commit).
# Flake budget (gh-1026): FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES=N makes the integration-mock
# stage rerun ONLY its failed files, up to N times, before failing — the
# load-sensitive PTY/grid timing legs stop costing a full 2.5 h leg per
# ambient flake (default 0 = single-shot, behaviour unchanged).
#
# CRAP ratchet scoping: in --hook mode the analyze runs over the STAGED
# lib/bin files only — the ratchet guards what a commit touches, so a
# pre-existing offender in an untouched file cannot block an unrelated
# commit. Non-hook runs (and ci.yml's whole-repo `crap4dart analyze`)
# keep the full-repo view, so nothing escapes the ratchet permanently.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

# Unset git env vars so test processes that spawn git subprocesses use the
# correct working directory rather than the hook's environment. The --hook
# scope detection below reads GIT_INDEX_FILE BEFORE this line runs.
SCOPE=auto
STAGES_OVERRIDE=""
HOOK_MODE=0
DRY_RUN=0
if [ "${GIT_INDEX_FILE:-}" ]; then HOOK_MODE=1; fi
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --scope) SCOPE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --scope=*) SCOPE="${1#*=}"; shift ;;
    --stages) STAGES_OVERRIDE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --stages=*) STAGES_OVERRIDE="${1#*=}"; shift ;;
    --hook) HOOK_MODE=1; shift ;;
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;   # print derived scope/stages, run nothing
    *) echo "Unknown argument: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done
unset GIT_DIR GIT_INDEX_FILE GIT_WORK_TREE 2>/dev/null || true

COVERAGE_BASELINE=80.0

119:#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
807:      # gh-2290: the watchdog's timeout-kill trip decision is
819:        run: bash scripts/watchdog_trip_selftest.sh
1326:    # without stretching the watchdog much.
1341:      # keys, post-merge on main) is small and the watchdog already hands
4116:  # Issue #194 (point 4): >2x-baseline watchdog. The timeout-minutes above
4124:  # this workflow receives, i.e. the release gate had NO watchdog at all.
4137:  watchdog:
4143:    # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
4145:    # retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
  watchdog:
    name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # pty-integration-linux/pty-visual ride along (review 2026-09-23, #963;
    # gh-1005 retired the mac shards): the longest legs. They must be in
    # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
    # timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot
    # retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, pty-integration-linux, pty-visual]
    # Same-repo PRs: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref. Tag pushes: the
    # release gate (gh-2290).
    if: always() && ((github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository) || (github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')))
    permissions:
      actions: write # gh workflow run — the tag-arm retrigger (gh-2290)
      contents: write
    steps:
      # gh-2290: the trip decision runs a REPO script — a hosted runner's
      # empty workspace has no scripts/ (the exit-127 class reddened the
      # dedupe pre-check on every arm, runs 38696670029/38696668627). The
      # checkout must be UNCONDITIONAL — the trip step runs on every arm
      # this job reaches, and a skipped checkout would empty the trip
      # output. Shallow: the script never reads history.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1

      # One jobs call in a SINGLE valid document (steps arrays are
      # embedded per job — no per-job follow-ups; `gh api --paginate`
      # concatenates page bodies and jq then reads only the first page —
      # verified against a 69-job run), then the extracted,
      # fixture-self-tested trip decision (scripts/watchdog_trip_check.sh;
      # static-gate selftest: scripts/watchdog_trip_selftest.sh). It trips
      # ONLY on the timeout-kill signature — job conclusion `failure` OR
      # `cancelled` (the v1.0.745 kill landed as plain `cancelled`) with
      # at least one `cancelled` step and NO `failed` step — and never on
      # a real test failure (a step failed, regardless of which step is
      # last), a skip, or a cancelled never-started job.
      - name: Detect a timeout-type failure
        id: trip
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          gh run view "$RUN_ID" --repo "$REPO" --json jobs > watchdog-jobs.json
          bash scripts/watchdog_trip_check.sh watchdog-jobs.json

      # ── PR arm: empty-commit push (unchanged remedy) ──────────────────
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: steps.trip.outputs.trip == 'true' && github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger workflows — the retrigger must
          # re-fire CI, so it rides RELEASE_PAT (same as release/gardener).
          token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}

      - name: Retrigger with an empty commit (fresh runner allocation)
        if: steps.trip.outputs.trip == 'true' && github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          HAS_PAT: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT != '' }}
        run: |
          if [ "$HAS_PAT" != "true" ]; then
            echo "::notice::RELEASE_PAT not configured — cannot retrigger"
            exit 0
          fi
          msg="ci: watchdog retrigger (degraded runner pool)"
          if [ "$(git log -1 --format=%s)" = "$msg" ]; then
            echo "head commit is already a watchdog retrigger — not looping"
            exit 0
          fi
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git commit --allow-empty -m "$msg"
          git push origin HEAD:"${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}"

      # ── Tag arm (gh-2290): dispatch a fresh gate run on the tag ref ────
      # ONE retrigger max per tag (issue #194 loop-guard rule): a prior
      # workflow_dispatch run for this tag ref means the retrigger already
      # fired for this kill — never chain dispatches on a stuck pool.
      - name: Retrigger the tag gate (dispatch, fresh runner allocation)
        if: steps.trip.outputs.trip == 'true' && github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          prior=$(gh run list --workflow ci.yml --branch "$REF" \
            --event workflow_dispatch \
            --json databaseId --jq 'length' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
          if [ "${prior:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "::notice::a workflow_dispatch gate run already exists for $REF — not re-firing (one retrigger max per tag, gh-2290)"
            exit 0
          fi
          gh workflow run ci.yml --ref "$REF"
          echo "::notice::dispatched a fresh ci.yml gate run on $REF (watchdog degraded-runner retrigger, gh-2290)"
  integration:
    name: Provider smoke (LLM, tag-only)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    # Same !cancelled() pattern as the release/binaries jobs (fa#456).
    # #1368: the gate check reads the dart_ok OUTPUT, not the aggregate
    # result — a platform-only red (Windows build, PTY leg) used to skip this
    # smoke transitively and with it the publish job (the v1.0.519-521
    # starvation). dart_ok=false (a red package leg) still skips it: the
    # publish it gates cannot run anyway.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.outputs.dart_ok != 'false' &&
      github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    env:
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

pty-integration-linux:
    # THE PR PTY/CLI integration leg (gh-1005: the former mac leg merged in;
    # before that, issue #931 part 2 sharded ONE ~40-min job into 3
    # duration-balanced shards — scripts/test_integration_shards.json,
    # file-level units). New integration-tagged files bin-pack in at runtime
    # (shard_files.py --tags integration), so a PR adding one never
    # silently skips it. Explicit --concurrency=4 bounds in-suite
    # parallelism (part 3.3 — package:test forbids `concurrency` in
    # dart_test.yaml tag overrides, so the knob lives here; it bounds
    # concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB — the rate-limit rationale is
    # documented on the llm tag in dart_test.yaml).
    # Per-shard coverage artifacts merge in pty-coverage-gate —
    # a single shard's ratchet would see partial lib/src/cli coverage
    # and false-regress. Each shard also emits the dart json
    # file-reporter: junit feeds rebalancing/budget-tightening PRs, the
    # raw json feeds the #928 duration gate (pty-coverage-gate below).
    # gh-1300: needs the once-per-run AOT build; FA_BIN points every CLI
    # spawn (PTY harness + headless helpers) at the prebuilt binary.
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, fa-aot-build]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    name: PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    # 40 > 30: the leg now carries the coverage + file-reporter overhead the
    # old mac leg had (the coverage-free linux twin never paid it) and arm64
    # Graviton cores run somewhat slower than the M-series minis did — margin
    # without stretching the watchdog much.
    timeout-minutes: 40
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2]
    env:
      # Secret shape (review 2026-09-23): this is the pull_request-time leg
      # that receives real provider secrets. GitHub withholds secrets from
      # forks, so external contributions never see them — but every
      # SAME-REPO branch runs this suite with the keys in its process
      # environment before human review (this repo's agent-authored-branch
      # model). The marginal escalation vs the nightly (same suites, same
      # keys, post-merge on main) is small and the watchdog already hands
      # RELEASE_PAT to same-repo PRs; documented here so the assumption is
      # explicit, not implicit.
      #
      # The live-provider legs (unlocked by these keys) load extra
      # lib/src/cli surface into the coverage measurement, so a no-key run
      # measures a DIFFERENT — lower-numbered — value; missing keys (forks)
      # self-skip those legs gracefully and the gate stays honest either
      # way.
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@2286a0c042b44434fe26d292bbce8d34f7ec662b # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # gh-1300: the AOT binary built once per run by fa-aot-build. The
      # guard FAILS the shard loudly if the artifact is missing or dead —
      # a silent JIT fallback would hide the optimization from AC1's
      # before/after numbers.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: fa-aot-bin
          path: fa-local/bundle
      # Artifact zips do NOT preserve the exec bit (download-artifact
      # README: "post-download the file is no longer guaranteed to be set
      # as an executable"). Run 37446280743: `test -x` below failed
      # silently ~20 ms in on EVERY shard — the gate went red before a
      # single test ran. Restore the mode the build job shipped; the
      # smoke below still verifies the restored binary is executable and
      # boots (never a silent JIT fallback). Content integrity is not
      # affected: download-artifact digest-validates (digest-mismatch:
      # error default), so this chmod only ever touches the verified
      # bundle the fa-aot-build job produced.
      - name: Restore exec bit (artifact zips drop permissions)
        run: chmod +x fa-local/bundle/bin/fa
      - name: Smoke the AOT binary (fail loud, never JIT-fallback)
        run: |
          test -x fa-local/bundle/bin/fa
          ./fa-local/bundle/bin/fa --version
      - name: dart test --tags integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
        env:
          # gh-1300 FA_BIN seam: every CLI spawn (pty_harness + the
          # headless helpers via faCliCommand) runs the AOT binary —
          # ~1 s per spawn instead of the JIT VM+CFE compile (~30 s on
          # loaded ARM runners). Per-test isolation is unchanged.
          FA_BIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-local/bundle/bin/fa
          # Issue #1391: stretch every PTY-harness wait budget 2x on this

OR the poll message can also appear... hmm, actually let me think again.

The message "Attempt:N waiting for isolate _waitForExitCode to check in" is emitted by the Dart VM when the VM is shutting down (or during an isolate group shutdown) and an isolate is stuck in native code (waitpid) and cannot reach a safepoint. Now, back to basics. The three hung tests are ALL PTY tests whose drivers are in the harness (`test/integration/pty_harness.dart`). The engine-level "Service connection disposed" crash is the NEW bit — has this happened before in this repo? Let me search the repo's docs/issues for "Service connection disposed" — and importantly, check whether this crash is related to **`--coverage` on the AOT binary**...

Hmm wait — actually, let me reconsider the whole thing once more. There's a much simpler hypothesis I haven't fully considered:

**The `collect()` call uses `forceCompile: true` on the SUITE ISOLATE while 3 other suite isolates are mid-test.** `getSourceReport` with forceCompile must PAUSE all isolates in the isolate group (compilation requires safepoints — actually getSourceReport forceCompile compiles pending libraries in the target isolate's group, requiring a safepoint across the GROUP). If some OTHER isolate (a suite mid-test, or pty2's `_waitForExitCode` isolate blocked in native waitpid) can't reach a safepoint, getSourceReport would... hang or fail — but "Service connection disposed"? The vm_service request times out after some period (default RPC timeout 80s? or unlimited?). Hmm, no — the crash happened 140ms after the last testDone, too quick for a hang.

Alternatively: **the suite isolate that just finished (resume_tail_grid) was being closed** (`resource.allowRelease(() => controller?.close())` in the finally AFTER writeCoverage — no, close happens after). Hmm.

Wait, actually — maybe I've got the ordering wrong: which suite's writeCoverage crashed? The trace doesn't say. Candidates: ANY suite whose tests were all done. The suite whose isolate's service connection was ALREADY disposed at its own writeCoverage time. If a suite's isolate exits IMMEDIATELY after its last test (before writeCoverage reads its coverage), you'd get exactly this: "Service connection disposed".

What if — the suite isolate CRASHED/exited abnormally mid-run (the three outstanding tests = the isolates that died)... Then:
- tui_protype_snapshot's isolate: outstanding test id 80.
- shell_job_countdown's isolate: outstanding test 93.
- ssh_shift_gate's isolate: outstanding test 98.

And resume_tail_grid (whose isolate finished normally) then hit the disposed connection. But a NORMAL suite isolate exit happens in `controller.close()` in the finally — AFTER writeCoverage. Unless the isolate exits ITSELF early.

  fa-aot-build:
    name: AOT fa binary (compiled once per run, gh-1300)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe]
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@2286a0c042b44434fe26d292bbce8d34f7ec662b # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-
      - run: dart pub get
      - uses: ./.github/actions/sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm
      - name: dart build cli (AOT bundle, same shape install_local.sh ships)
        run: |
          dart build cli --target=bin/fa.dart --output=fa-local
          version=$(git describe --tags --always --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo 0.0.0-dev)
          version="${version#v}"
          echo "$version" > fa-local/bundle/version.txt
          ./fa-local/bundle/bin/fa --version
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:

          path: fa-local/bundle/

env:
          # gh-1300 FA_BIN seam: every CLI spawn (pty_harness + the
          # headless helpers via faCliCommand) runs the AOT binary —
          # ~1 s per spawn instead of the JIT VM+CFE compile (~30 s on
          # loaded ARM runners). Per-test isolation is unchanged.
          FA_BIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-local/bundle/bin/fa
          # Issue #1391: stretch every PTY-harness wait budget 2x on this
          # merge-blocking leg. SM dispatch waves pack the hosted-arm pool
          # (refresh waves supersede PR heads mid-run), and drilled reds
          # are all single tests popping quiet-runner budgets inside
          # otherwise-green 60-70-test shards. Local runs and the nightly
          # leave the var unset and keep the exact legacy budgets (the
          # nightly's unsupervised verdicts feed quarantine decisions).
          FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE: '2'
        run: |
          # gh-1199 AC1: --exclude-tag llm keeps every live-provider file
          # out of the merge-blocking selection (manifest unit AND runtime
          # bin-pack); --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm is the dart-test
          # backstop. AC6: the quarantine filter drops flake-quarantined
          # files (scripts/test_quarantine.json) pending their fix PRs.
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }} --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py)
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          if [ -z "$targets" ]; then
            echo "shard fully quarantined — nothing to run"
            exit 0
          fi
          mkdir -p build/test-results
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm \
            --concurrency=4 \
            --coverage=coverage \
            --file-reporter="json:build/test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
      # The file-reporter writes the json even on a RED leg — convert +
      # upload must not be chained into the failing step (#928 review):
      # timing evidence is exactly what red runs need to keep.
      - name: junit durations (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: always()
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py
          build/test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          build/test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
      # Raw dart json for the #928 duration gate (per-test spans incl. suite
      # paths); junit is the human/rebalancer-facing form of the same data.
      # Upload MUST stay on the current upload-artifact line (gh-995): the
      # gate's download-artifact v8 digest-validates every download, so an
      # old-line upload digest-mismatches and the shard merge loses its
      # report (test/gh995_artifact_action_pins_test.dart pins the pin).
      #
      # gh-1412: each evidence upload carries a one-shot retry (the step
      # right after it, same pinned action). The gh-1412 validation run
      # 37807820733 red'd a shard whose 68 tests ALL passed on a single
      # transient `Failed to FinalizeArtifact: ECONNRESET` from GitHub's
      # blob storage — the aggregate gate followed and the merge aborted.
      # The retry re-runs the SAME action with overwrite:true (a failed
      # attempt leaves the artifact half-registered — without overwrite the
      # retry dies on "already exists"); a genuinely dead endpoint still
      # fails the shard loudly, and the retries stay if: always()-reachable

content.thinking:
The ssh_shift_gate test uses `FaCliHarness.spawn`, `waitForBoot`, `waitForText(timeout: 30s)`. If `waitForText` times out, it throws — test fails (not hangs). So how would this test HANG indefinitely? The PTY harness wait budgets: FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE=2. The hang was indefinite (39 min with no timeout) — so the hang is NOT inside waitForText (it has timeouts). The hang must be in the pty2 native wait — i.e., the wedge at shutdown/exit.

Reconsider: at t≈31.4s the coverage collect crashed. THEN at t≈43s the VM started its exit-time check-in wait (attempt 1 ≈ 02:51:43, t≈32.5s actually — let me recompute: attempt 11 at 02:51:53.59, so attempt 1 at 02:51:43.6, t≈33s; attempt counter increments every ~1s: attempt 2329 at 03:30:32). So VM exit began at t≈33s, 1.5s after the coverage crash. That fits: the crash propagated → engine.run() failed → main() failed → VM exit began at ~t=33s → exit wedged on `_waitForExitCode` isolate.

Now the exit wedge: pty2's BlockingPseudoTerminal._waitForExitCode isolate blocked in native waitpid on a LIVE child. The three outstanding tests had live PTY children (their tests never completed → tearDowns never ran → children alive). At VM exit, those `_waitForExitCode` isolates can't check in. VM waits FOREVER (the check-in attempt loop). Hence the 40-min timeout.

So BOTH symptoms share one trigger: the run ABORTED at t≈31.4s while tests were still running. The trigger is the "getSourceReport: Service connection disposed" unhandled error. Everything after is consequence.

So the REAL bug: why did getSourceReport fail with a disposed connection 140ms after resume_tail_grid's last testDone?

Hmm wait — actually, WHICH suite's writeCoverage crashed? Not necessarily resume_tail. Any suite that completed. But 140ms after the LAST testDone strongly suggests it was resume_tail_grid's (its tests just finished).

Now — why would the vm service connection be disposed? Consider: THREE suites were mid-test (hung tests in tui_protype/countdown/ssh_shift_gate). WAIT — were those tests hung, though? Maybe they were just SLOW (PTY tests take seconds each). tui_protype's test 80 started ~t=21.3s; crash at t=31.4s — 10s in-flight, plausible for a slow test (FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE=2 doubles budgets).

Hmm OK here's another thought — the service connection: `collect(serviceUri, ...)` — the serviceUri belongs to the MAIN process's VM service. package:coverage opens a NEW websocket per collect() call. The harness has `shutdownPty` for normal teardowns, but an abrupt VM exit (unhandled engine crash) skips tearDowns entirely → children outlive → wedge.

Now, the KEY decision: what is the FIX for this ticket?

The observed incident:
1. v1.0.75's Quality gate went red because PTY shard 2/3 was killed at its 40-min job timeout.
2. The kill happened because the run FROZE: an unhandled `getSourceReport: Service connection disposed` error at t≈31s aborted the engine, and the VM exit then wedged forever on pty2's waitpid-blocked `_waitForExitCode` isolate (in-flight tests' children never reaped because tearDowns never ran).
3. Same code passed on the retriggered run — the crash itself is a rare race (degraded/load class), NOT a deterministic regression from 21a06bc.

What can/should this bug leg actually change? Options:

**Option A: nothing to fix in code; report as flake + rely on the watchdog retrigger** (the retrigger already fired and the gate is going green). But the ticket explicitly asks the dev leg to fix the CI red. The pipeline will close the ticket "when the ref goes green" — the retrigger is doing that. Still, the leg should deliver analysis + a hardening fix that prevents the 40-min-burn class.

**Option B: harden the wedge** — the genuinely fixable defect: when the runner aborts, the process must not hang forever. Two layers:
  1. **In the harness**: a best-effort reaper that force-kills live PTY children at VM exit — but Dart cannot run code at process exit if the exit is a VM-handshake wedge... Actually it CAN: the wedge happens because the VM waits for the stuck isolates DURING exit; main() already returned (with the error). There's no Dart hook that runs after main returns. BUT we can prevent the wedge differently: make sure every spawned CLI child is BOUND to the test's lifetime via `addTearDown` (already done) AND additionally kill children when the test's zone closes... tearDown already does that. The abrupt-exit case (unhandled error at engine level) skips tearDowns — unavoidable from test code.
   
  2. **In CI (ci.yml / a wrapper)**: run the dart test command under a bounded wall-clock that SIGKILLs on hang — turning a 40-min timeout burn into a fast, LOUD red (which the leg then reports as a normal red leg, and... the aggregate goes red immediately instead of after 40 min). Hmm — but a red shard still reds the gate. The improvement: (a) 40 min → ~few min wall cost; (b) the failure becomes a REAL test failure (step failure) instead of a timeout-kill signature — the watchdog would NOT retrigger (no point re-triggering a deterministic failure... but this failure class IS transient — a retrigger is exactly the right remedy; keeping the timeout-kill signature lets the watchdog auto-heal). Hmm, careful: don't break the watchdog semantics.

  3. **Reduce the blast radius of the coverage crash itself**: The unhandled error propagated out of Engine.run's FutureGroup because test_core doesn't guard the per-suite writeCoverage. That's a test_core bug (the message even says "Please file an issue"). We can't fix test_core, but we CAN remove the trigger: per-suite coverage collection racing with in-flight suites. CI runs `--coverage=coverage` on the WHOLE shard. The coverage crash happened when collect(forceCompile: true) ran on a suite isolate while OTHER suites mid-flight held native-blocked isolates... (unproven, but plausible).

Actually — hold on. Let me look for what actually CHANGED to make this fail NOW. The green run at 02:27 (main) ran the same shard with the same command on the same SDK and passed. The failing run 31 seconds in — a race that needs load/timing to trigger. The retrigger passed. So: transient.

Given the repo's OWN conventions (watchdog gh-2290, quarantine policy, gh-2072 precedent for a transient-error class getting a retry+belt), the highest-value, MINIMUM, targeted fix for THIS incident is:

**Make the PTY shard's dart test step resilient to the wedged-exit class: bound the dart test step's wall clock with an external SIGKILL (e.g., `timeout --kill-after=... <budget> dart test ...`)**, so when the VM wedges on the check-in handshake, the step turns into a bounded, prompt red — with the artifact uploads still running (they're separate steps) — instead of a 40-minute runner hostage. Wait — but the job-level timeout (40 min) ALREADY does this, just slower. The bounded wrapper turns 40 min into, say, 45+2 min? Hmm — what budget? The dart test step legitimately runs up to ~35 min when the suite is slow-but-progressing. A wrapper budget must exceed the legitimate duration. The junit durations (from the artifacts) show per-shard historical durations. If shard 2 legitimately takes ~25-30 min... a wrapper can't safely be much tighter than the job timeout. Gain: small.

Hmm. Reconsider: is there something that bounds the WEDGE itself? The wedge = VM waiting for isolates to check in at exit. Is there a Dart VM flag to bound that wait? ... There's `--isolate-group-*`? I don't recall a flag bounding exit handshake. 

**Prevent the children from being alive at exit at all**: the wedge needs (a) VM exiting + (b) live child with a waitpid isolate. (a) was triggered by the unhandled coverage error. If (a) is fixed, (b) never happens. Fix (a): the coverage crash is INSIDE test_core → unfixable directly... BUT we could stop using per-suite coverage collection on this leg? The PTY coverage feeds `pty-coverage-gate` (ratchet). Removing coverage would break the ratchet. No.

Hmm, what about the ACTUAL trigger race? Let me dig one more level: WHY was the service connection disposed? # Vendored: pty2

- **Upstream**: https://github.com/jtmcdole/termui/tree/main/packages/pty2
  (pub.dev `pty2 0.5.7`, MIT — see LICENSE).
- **Why vendored**: gh-2208 — pty2's `BlockingPseudoTerminal` runs a
  `_waitForExitCode` isolate blocked in a native FFI `waitpid` with no
  timeout. While a PTY child lives, that isolate can neither reach a
  safepoint nor answer the Dart VM's exit-time check-in handshake, so the
  whole `dart test` process wedges forever
  (`Attempt:N waiting for isolate _waitForExitCode to check in` — CI runs
  43835937617 / v1.0.735 and 43151400571 / PR #2121; tracker issue #2122).
  The PTY test harness (`test/integration/pty_harness.dart`) needs the
  child pid to SIGKILL-escalate when the cooperative `kill()` (SIGTERM +
  SIGHUP, once-only per pty2's `_killed` flag) does not reap the child
  within its grace window — otherwise a leaked child turns the CI leg
  into a 40-minute zombie.
- **Patch vs upstream 0.5.7** (the only diff): the `pid` getter is exposed
  end-to-end — `PtyCore.pid` + `PseudoTerminal.pid` interface members,
  `BasePseudoTerminal.pid`/`PtyCoreUnix.pid` delegating to the existing
  private `_pid`, and `PtyCoreWindows.pid` via `GetProcessId(_hProcess)`
  (upstream's commented-out shape returned the process HANDLE, not the
  pid). `pubspec.yaml`: dropped the upstream `resolution: workspace`
  marker (this repo is not a pub workspace). Everything else is verbatim.
- **Consumers**: the root package's dev_dependencies (`pubspec.yaml`,
  `pty2: {path: vendor/pty2}` — staged like `vendor/xterm`, CI run
  43851264755); `flutter_app` keeps the hosted 0.5.7 — behavior identical,
  the patch adds getters only.
- **Un-vendor when**: upstream exposes `pid` in a release; bump the
  dev-dep back to the hosted constraint and delete this directory.

content.thinking:
Now I see pty2's structure:

- `BlockingPseudoTerminal.init()` spawns TWO isolates: `_waitForExitCode` (blocking `waitpid` via `ctx.arg.exitCodeBlocking()`) and `_readUntilExit` (blocking `read()`).
- `_readUntilExit` also blocks in native `read()` — it too can't check in while the child lives (the PTY master fd stays open → read blocks until the child exits and the slave side drains).

At VM exit, BOTH isolates are stuck in native code. The exit handshake waits for all isolates in the group.

Can PDEATHSIG help here? PDEATHSIG kills the CHILD when the parent dies. `waitpid` returns once the child is dead (it's our child — waitpid succeeds immediately; the zombie gets reaped). `read()` on the PTY master: when the child dies, the slave side closes; readers get EIO/EOF once the buffer drains → read returns → isolate proceeds. So yes — if the child dies at parent death, both stuck isolates unblock quickly, and the VM exit handshake completes. THE WEDGE DISSOLVES.

Where to set PDEATHSIG? In the child, before/after exec. pty2's Unix core: let me look at how it spawns (fork/exec in native FI? posix_spawn?).

content.thinking:
The vendored pty2 does a raw `fork()` + `execve()` in the child with async-signal-safe calls only. Adding **PR_SET_PDEATHSIG** in the child (before execve) is straightforward:

```dart
@Native<Int32 Function(Int32, Int32, ...)>(symbol: 'prctl', isLeaf: true)
external int _nativePrctl(int option, int arg2);

// In the child, after setsid:
_nativePrctl(1 /* PR_SET_PDEATHSIG */, 9 /* SIGKILL */);
``

CRITICAL caveat: PDEATHSIG fires when the parent **THREAD** dies. After `setsid()`, the child is reparented... no wait, setsid makes the child a session leader but it still has the same PARENT. If the forking OS thread exits before the process exits, the child gets SIGKILL prematurely — the Dart VM spawns processes on a pool thread; that thread lives until process end in practice (the fork happens synchronously within start() on the calling isolate's thread — Dart isolates run on VM thread pool threads; if the isolate that called PtyCoreUnix.start completes and its thread returns to the pool WITHOUT dying... the thread doesn't die when an isolate finishes — it's a pool thread. The risk of thread death is low: pool threads persist for the VM's lifetime. Hmm, but they CAN be shut down when idle after a timeout? The Dart VM's thread pool: threads can exit when idle (MLRS). If the thread that forked exits later while the process still lives and the child still runs → the child dies prematurely → test breaks (PTY child killed mid-test). That's a REAL risk — pool threads DO retire when idle.

Wait, do they? The Dart VM uses a thread pool; idle threads park on condition variables, they don't exit... Actually the VM's ThreadPool: `ThreadPool::Worker` threads stay alive parked (they don't terminate) — I believe workers persist (there's a max count, and idle workers park). Dart VM's thread pool workers DO NOT exit when idle (they park). OK but there's also the classic race: parent dies BETWEEN fork and prctl — handle by checking getppid() after prctl and self-killing if it changed. In the child: after prctl, `if (_nativeGetppid() != parentPid) _nativeKill(self, 9)`. Hmm, requires getppid binding. Async-signal-safe: fine.

Now — the BIG question: is this the RIGHT fix, or is it over-reach for this ticket? Scope check per the TDD rules: "NEVER fix code without a failing reproduction test first" and "make minimum targeted fix for the root cause ONLY".

The root cause chain has THREE layers:
1. **Trigger (upstream toolchain race)**: test_core per-suite coverage collect → `getSourceReport: Service connection disposed` → engine abort. NOT fixable here (dart-lang/test#1423/#225 territory).
2. **Amplifier 1 (tearDown skip)**: the abort skips tearDowns → live children. Not fixable at test level (no code runs).
3. **Amplifier 2 (unbounded VM exit handshake)**: waitpid-blocked isolates wedge the exit for 40 min until the job timeout kills everything. **Fixable here**: if children die at parent death, the handshake completes in seconds and the leg exits red in ~1 min.

With fix 3, this incident's cost profile: red leg in ~1 min, artifacts upload, gate reds, ci-red-report files the ticket... same as now but 40× cheaper and WITHOUT the timeout-kill signature (a clean step failure instead). Hmm — and the watchdog would NOT auto-retrigger (step failure ≠ timeout signature)... but that's FINE: the retrigger remedy exists for DEGRADED RUNERS; a coverage race isn't runner-degradation... though actually a retrigger WOULD still be the right remedy (transient). The watchdog's classification would see: job conclusion `failure`, with the dart-test step `failure` — "a real test failure" signature — no retrigger. The leg would just red the release again until a human/agent re-rolls. Hmm — is losing auto-heal acceptable? 

Alternative wrapper that PRESERVES auto-heal AND cuts the burn: put the SIGKILL escalation INSIDE the step with the right exit-code dance? If the wrapper kills dart test AND exits with a special code that... the step's conclusion is driven by exit code (non-zero = failure; only runner-level cancellation produces `cancelled`). Can't fake `cancelled` from within the step (well — `::error` + exit... no).

Hmm — what about a middle path: **fix the wedge (PDEATHSIG) so the VM exits promptly**, and leave the watchdog as-is. On a future wedge-class incident: leg reds in ~1 min with the coverage-crash evidence; the ci-red-report auto-files a ticket (as it did now); a human/ai leg can re-roll CI. The 40-min hostage disappears. The one-shot-retrigger automation is reserved for degraded runners — arguably the right classification anyway.

Hmm, wait — but actually, would the PDEATHSIG fix even fire in THIS incident? The wedge happens at VM exit — the parent process does NOT die during the handshake (it's alive, waiting). PDEATHSIG fires only when the parent dies. During the handshake the parent is alive → children stay alive → handshake still wedges!! 

NO WAIT — re-think. PDEATHSIG fires when the parent THREAD dies. During the exit handshake, the process is alive (all threads alive, parked). So the child survives, waitpid still blocks, the handshake STILL wedges. **PDEATHSIG does NOT fix this wedge.** It would only help for SIGKILL-from-outside cases (parent killed by the runner — but the runner already kills the whole tree then). So PDEATHSIG is USELESS here. Good catch — dropped.

What ACTUALLY unblocks the handshake? The child must DIE (so waitpid returns) or the stuck isolate must unblock. Who can kill the child? Only the test process (which is wedged mid-handshake — no Dart code runs) or an external process. So the only in-repo remedy: **an external babysitter that kills the children when the parent stops progressing** — e.g., the CI step runs `dart test` under a supervisor that watches stdout progress and SIGKILLs on stall... complex.

OR — kill the children at Dart level BEFORE the handshake: can't (no code runs).

OR — prevent the ENGINE ABORT in the first place (fix the trigger): if writeCoverage's error doesn't propagate fatally, tearDowns run, children get reaped, exit is clean. The error is thrown INSIDE test_core's closure... but WAIT — what if the crash is avoidable by CHANGING HOW COVERAGE IS COLECTED on this leg? The leg uses `--coverage=coverage` (per-suite collect with forceCompile). What if we collect coverage OUT-OF-BAND instead: run dart test WITHOUT --coverage, and separately run `coverage:collect` against... no, that requires the service URI / paused VM.

Hmm what about `--coverage` + the `-j 1` suite-concurrency knob? The crash is a race between concurrent coverage collects (multiple suites finishing → concurrent collect() calls → concurrent getSourceReport on different isolates → VM service connection disposed). With `-j 1` (one suite at a time), collects serialize... but collect() is called in the per-suite closure while OTHER suites' tests are mid-flight only when suite concurrency > 1. With -j 1: suite N finishes → its closure runs writeCoverage while NO other suite runs tests → much less race surface. Cost: suite serialization slows the shard (but --concurrency=4 still runs 4 tests... no — tests within DIFFERENT suites wouldn't overlap; each suite is one file; the shard's wall time ≈ sum of file durations with 4-way test-parallelism only within a file — most files are sequential test lists... that would INCREASE shard wall time significantly, risking more timeout kills. Not great.

WAIT. Which connection got disposed? A NEWLY-OPENED connection that died within 140ms. For a NEW ws connection to die immediately: the VM service REJECTED it or the service is shutting down. Hmm — what if the VM service was BUSY/overloaded... 

You know what? I've hit diminishing returns on the crash internals. Let me now also reconsider a COMPLETELY different remedy frame — one that matches the repo's established doctrine EXACTLY (gh-2072 precedent):

The equivalent here: **the coverage gather crash is a known-transient in the merge-blocking leg with NO retry**. The house remedy = a bounded CI-level retry of the RED leg (the same "flake budget" pattern as FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES in the fast gate's integration-mock stage!). The fast gate already has FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES=N: "makes the integration-mock stage rerun ONLY its failed files, up to N times, before failing". And there's `dart test --rerun-failed`?? Hmm — dart test doesn't have --rerun-failed... Actually the ci.yml mentions "gh-220: rerun --failed never fires the gh-1412 retry" — let me look at how gh-220's rerun-failed works. If dart test supports retrying failed files, a retry shim could rerun the shard on a transient ABORT... but an ABORT (process died without a junit report) isn't a "failed test" — it's a crashed run. Retry criterion: the json/junit artifact missing or incomplete + nonzero exit → rerun once.

{"body":"## What happened

`PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard 2/3)`, run 43151400571 (2026-11-12, PR #2121): all **81 tests in the shard passed in ~30 s** (03:57:30 → 03:57:57), then the leg hung for **36+ minutes** until the run was superseded:

- 03:57:58 — coverage collection starts (`package:coverage collect → getSourceReport`, stack in the log);
- 03:58:09 → 04:34:49 — the log fills with **4,400 lines** of `Attempt:N waiting for isolate _waitForExitCode to check in`, attempts reaching **#2210** (~2 lines/second);
- the run was cancelled by a superseding push; post-cancel cleanup terminated orphan `dart:concatenat` / `dart:dartdev_ao` processes.

Sibling evidence on IDENTICAL content, same image (`macos-26-arm64` image `20261102.0473.1` in all cases), same SDKs:

- run 43147985274 (30 min earlier): all three PTY shards green in **~2.5 min** each;
- run 43155863851 (35 min later, same head content): PTY shard 2 green in the normal envelope;
- a full `--update-goldens` capture on the same hosted pool rendered 396 baselines **byte-identical** minutes after the hang.

## Root cause — upstream, not our harness

`Attempt:N waiting for isolate <name> to check in` is a **Dart VM-internal isolate spawn/check-in handshake** retry loop (the string is compiled into `dartaotruntime` / `flutter_tester`). The stalled isolate here is named `_waitForExitCode` — package:test_core's helper isolate that waits for a suite isolate's exit code.

Known upstream class, open since 2021:

- dart-lang/sdk#45771 — `Attempt:xxx waiting for isolate vm-isolate to check in` (dart migrate)
- dart-lang/sdk#46255 — `Attempt:11 waiting for isolate vm-isolate to check in`
- flutter/flutter#80739 — same signature

We cannot fix the VM handshake from this repo. What we CAN decide, with eyes open:

1. Nothing (accept rare multi-minute burns; they self-heal on retry) — status quo.
2. A bounded wait around the coverage-bearing `dart test` legs so a stall fails fast instead of zombie-ing the runner pool — rejected as a band-aid for now per owner call; if it recurs at cost, revisit as a deliberate policy.
3. Investigate whether the stall correlates with coverage collection load (`getSourceReport` in flight when the handshake starves) — e.g. run one shard with `--coverage` off as a data point.

## Evidence pointers

- red job log: run 43151400571, job 130961615719 (line ~547 for the attempt storm, ~530 for the coverage stack)
- green siblings: run 43147985274 jobs 130950779014.., run 43155863851 (PTY shard","comments":3,"labels":["ai_developed"],"state":"open","title":"PTY integration CI: dart VM isolate spawn/check-in stall — Attempt:N waiting for isolate _waitForExitCode to check in (36+ min hang, upstream dart-lang/sdk class)"}

# Root Cause Analysis — gh-2335 `[ci-red] v1.0.755 failed` (Quality gate)

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The `Quality gate` aggregate on the v1.0.755 tag push (CI run
44663474678) failed because the `PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard 2/3)`
leg was killed at its 40-minute job timeout and the aggregate counts
`cancelled` as red (`R_PTY_LINUX: cancelled` → "a platform/native leg is
red — the aggregate is red").

**Root cause** (evidence: shard log + the uploaded `integration-json-shard-2.json`
file-reporter, run 44663474678, job 136047522662):

1. Shard 2/3 started `dart test --tags integration … --coverage=coverage` at
   02:51:04Z; 25 suites targeted, 15 loaded, 68 tests started.
2. At **02:51:41.89Z** (t≈31 s), the per-suite coverage gather crashed with an
   unhandled exception: `getSourceReport: (-32000) Service connection disposed`
   (`package:coverage collect → test_core runner_suite.gatherCoverage →
   engine.dart:303`). This is the known upstream `dart test --coverage` crash
   class (dart-lang/test#1423 "Tests hang at coverage command", dart-lang/test#2255,
   closed-as-duplicate). The abort happened with **3 tests still outstanding**
   (tui_prototype_snapshot "typing text and pressing Enter submits",
   shell_job_countdown_pty "ten background bash jobs", ssh_shift_gate "SSH
   session env: the first Enter submits") and 10 suites never loaded — the
   engine died mid-run, so their tearDowns never ran.
3. Because the aborted tests' PTY children were never reaped, pty2's
   `_waitForExitCode` isolates stayed blocked in native `waitpid`. From
   02:51:43Z the log fills with `Attempt:N waiting for isolate _waitForExitCode
   to check in` (one line/second for 39 minutes, attempts reaching #2351) —
   the Dart VM's exit-time check-in handshake wedge documented in
   flutter_agent_harness#2122 (upstream dart-lang/sdk#45771 class). No Dart
   code runs during the handshake, so no in-repo teardown can fire.
4. 03:30:54Z — the job's `timeout-minutes: 40` killed the shard
   (conclusion `cancelled`, step `cancelled`, no failed step).
5. The aggregate `quality-gate` job evaluated `R_PTY_LINUX: cancelled` and
   failed: "Quality gate FAILED: a platform/native leg is red". All other
   legs were success/skipped; `dart_ok=true` (the publish gate was never
   blocked).

Classification: **CI-infrastructure transient, not a product regression.**
Commit 21a06bc (the only commit between the green main-branch schedule run
44660879631 at 02:27Z and the red tag run at 02:49Z) touches Copilot provider
code that runs inside the CLI **subprocess**; the crash is in the test
runner's own VM service connection, and the wedge is in test-process pty2
isolates — subprocess code cannot dispose the runner's service connection.
The crash+hang shape matches the pre-existing, owner-triaged class in
flutter_agent_harness#2122 ("all tests passed in ~30 s, then the coverage
gather + attempt storm"); v1.0.735 run 43835937617, PR #2121 run 43151400571
and v1.0.745 are prior occurrences. Issue #2122 records the owner call:
status quo — accept rare burns, they self-heal on retry; bounded-wait
band-aids explicitly rejected.

**Impact**: One-off red release gate; 40 runner-minutes burned on a wedged
shard; release blocked until re-roll. Deterministically non-reproducible:
same SHA, fresh runner → all green.

**Fix approach**: No product/code change — root cause is upstream (VM exit
handshake × test_core coverage gather), and the self-heal already exists:
the gh-2290 watchdog tripped the timeout-kill signature
(`PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard 2/3): cancelled (cancelled step: dart
test …)`) and dispatched a fresh gate run on the tag ref
(run 44668292567, 03:31:20Z). That run completed **success** — every leg
including all three PTY/CLI integration shards and the Quality gate — so the
ref v1.0.755 is green, which is the ticket's closure condition ("Closes
manually when the ref goes green").

## Verification

- Local reproduction attempt of the EXACT failing scope (same shard target
  list, same flags: `--concurrency=4 --coverage --file-reporter=json`,
  `FA_BIN` AOT binary, `FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE=2`) against the current tree:
  PASS — the failure does not reproduce.
- CI: retriggered run 44668292567 on the same tag — Quality gate **success**;
  PTY/CLI integration shards 0/3, 1/3, 2/3 all **success**.

## Previous attempt

None — first dev leg on this ticket.

## Notes

- Evidence for issue #2122's open option 3 (coverage-correlation data point):
  in this occurrence the coverage gather did not merely precede the storm —
  it crashed first (`Service connection disposed`) and the abort itself is
  what stranded the unreaped children. Prior #2122 occurrences hung without
  the crash (all tests green). Worth keeping on file for a future
  deliberate policy change.

arguments.content:
### Root Cause

- `Quality gate` red on run [44663474678](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/44663474678) = the aggregate counting a red platform leg: `PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard 2/3)` was killed at its 40-minute job timeout (`R_PTY_LINUX: cancelled`).
- At t≈31 s the shard aborted mid-run with an upstream `dart test --coverage` crash — `getSourceReport: (-32000) Service connection disposed` (dart-lang/test#1423 class) — leaving 3 tests' PTY children unreaped; pty2's `_waitForExitCode` isolates then blocked the VM exit handshake (`Attempt:N waiting for isolate _waitForExitCode to check in`, 39 min of storm) until the timeout kill.
- Known, owner-triaged class: flutter_agent_harness#2122 (prior hits: v1.0.735 run 43835937617, PR #2121 run 43151400571, v1.0.745). Upstream VM/test_core territory — not fixable in this repo; #2122 records the owner call: status quo, self-heals on retry.

### Fix

- **No code change** (per the #2122 owner decision; commit `21a06bc` is not implicated — it only touches Copilot provider code inside the CLI subprocess, and the crash lives in the test runner's own VM service connection).
- The built-in self-heal already fired: the gh-2290 watchdog tripped the timeout-kill signature and dispatched a fresh gate run on the tag → run [44668292567](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/44668292567) completed **success** (all three PTY/CLI integration shards + Quality gate green). **The ref v1.0.755 is green** — the ticket's closure condition.

### Test Coverage

- Local re-run of the exact failing shard's target list with the CI flags (AOT `FA_BIN`, `FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE=2`, `--concurrency=4`, `--coverage`, json file-reporter): **82 passed**; 7 initial local failures were traced to this sandbox leaking `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` (a real glm provider queue) into the spawned CLI — with the CI-shaped env the same tests pass **9/9**.
- CI same-SHA re-run: PTY/CLI integration shards 0/3, 1/3, 2/3 → **success**.

### Notes

- Evidence for #2122's open coverage-correlation item (option 3): in this occurrence the coverage gather did not merely precede the stall — it **crashed first** and the abort itself stranded the unreaped children; earlier #2122 occurrences hung with all tests green.
- No regression risk introduced; working tree left clean (analysis-only leg, no commits).
